analysis.title: US Equities - back to panic (Lee Coppersmith, 6 Nov 2026)
key_insights: GS Vol Panic Index surged to 9.57 out of 10 on 5 Nov, back in the panic zone (9.5+). The roughly 5pt rise was the 3rd largest daily jump ever, following Wednesday's drop that was the 4th largest ever. The two-day swing was the largest on record.

Clients sold protection into Wednesday's post-midterm relief rally and were materially underhedged going into Thursday's reversal. Equities unwound, hedge funds faced forced liquidations, and the market scrambled to buy back protection it had just sold.
The 10-day volatility of the Vol Panic Index reached an all-time high. VVIX had its 2nd largest one-day increase ever, behind only the Feb 2018 Volmageddon.

VIX is in the high 20s, but Nasdaq's VXN hit its highest level since Liberation Day and had its biggest one-day repricing since Covid. The whole VIX curve flipped from contango to sharp backwardation.
Cboe traded more than 11 million puts on 5 Nov, the largest put volume day on record, above the prior high in Apr 2025. Index puts led, and single-stock put volume was the 4th highest day ever.

Hedge fund losses on 5 Nov: fundamental L/S -1.3% (-2 SD), US funds -1.7%, TMT funds down more than 4%, multi-strats -1.4%, momentum a 3.7 SD move. Systematic L/S was +0.2%. TMT managers are roughly flat YTD versus +24% before the summer AI unwind.

After the prior 15 Vol Panic signals above 9.5, the S&P averaged +4.6% over 3 months (80% hit rate) and +9.0% over 6 months (73% hit rate). The near-term path has been less reliable while the market is still in price discovery.

The midterms added political and regulatory uncertainty to the AI buildout. Texas is 20%/27% of under-construction US data center additions in 2027/28, and possible moratoriums raise timing and cost concerns. GS argues delays would extend the construction cycle rather than impair the opportunity.

GS Research raised its US data center construction spending forecasts to $80bn/$100bn in 2026/27 and expects $125bn in 2028. About $300bn of construction is under way, and the high-probability pipeline takes that closer to $900bn.

Coppersmith reads 5 Nov as largely a poor technical setup and forced re-hedging rather than a fundamental deterioration. Near-term tails remain large and more positioning needs to be worked through. He says it is getting harder to ignore the opportunity as forced selling runs its course, but not necessarily a reason to rush back into risk.

sector_views.rationale: Political and regulatory uncertainty from the midterms threatens project timing, but GS Research sees spending visibility through 2028 and treats delays as extending the cycle rather than cancelling it.

tension_points.bull_case: Panic readings at historical extremes have preceded S&P gains of 4.6% over 3m and 9.0% over 6m. The selloff looks like a technical and forced re-hedging event, and data center spending visibility runs through 2028.
tension_points.bear_case: The near-term tails remain unusually large, more positioning is still to be worked through, and the immediate path has been unreliable while in price discovery. The midterms add regulatory uncertainty to AI spending.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Further forced selling and re-hedging while the market is still in price discovery would delay the setup. The report names no specific level.

theme_stances.key_argument: With panic readings at historical extremes and spending still healthy, the setup looks more interesting as forced selling runs its course.
theme_stances.evidence: harder to ignore the potential opportunity on the other side

theme_stances.key_argument: Delays could extend the construction cycle rather than materially impair the opportunity.
